claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'll be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions since he's 18 years old.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** For example, is he enrolled in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or equivalent) or an approved training program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't gone on to do A-levels or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question:

**When did Alex turn 18?** I need to know the specific date or at least which month he turned 18, as this affects eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 18 back in February this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 18 years old (turned 18 in February this year)
- He is not currently in approved education or training
- He lives at home with you

I now have enough information to make a determination.

conversation.text:
## **Eligibility Decision for Alex: INELIGIBLE**

I'm sorry, but you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

Under UK Child Benefit rules, Child Benefit generally stops when a child turns 16. However, it can continue beyond age 16 if the young person remains in approved full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels or Scottish Highers) or approved training. In those cases, Child Benefit can continue until they turn 20, or until the 31st August after their 19th birthday, whichever comes first.

Since Alex is 18 years old and is not currently in any approved education or training, he does not meet the criteria for Child Benefit. His eligibility would have ended either when he turned 16 or at the end of the school term after he left education.

**Important:** If Alex's circumstances change and he enrolls in approved full-time education or training in the future, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again, provided he is still under 20 years old at the time.

If you have any other questions or if his situation changes, please feel free to reach out.
